Indigenous Health Assessment (Adults 15–54 years)  
Patient: Sarah Smith | DOB: 20 Apr 1980 (clinician later stated 1983 – conflict noted)  

Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • Sudden onset shortness of breath while resting (≈1 hour duration).  
  • Non-productive cough started yesterday.  
  • Post-cesarean section 4 weeks ago → postpartum venous thrombo-embolism risk.  
  • Reports palpitations; chest feels sore on deep inspiration and around C-section scar.

- Relevant family medical history:
  • Mother has history of leg clots (venous thrombosis).

- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Codeine (analgesic) – dose/route/frequency not documented; taken regularly until 1 week ago; instructed to withhold further doses.  
  • No other medications reported.

- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.

- Sexual and reproductive health:
  • Gave birth via C-section 4 weeks ago.  
  • Infant currently well.  
  • No other reproductive or sexual health information documented.

- Physical activity and nutrition: Not recorded.

- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: Not recorded.

- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.

- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):
  • Feels “really stressed” due to current episode; no formal screening performed.

- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.

- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:
  • Lives with partner (at work during call); primary carer for newborn.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  
  • Patient counted 30 beats over clinician-directed interval; clinician described result as “slightly fast.” Exact rate, rhythm, and BP not recorded.

- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference: Not recorded.

- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not recorded.

- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded.

- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not recorded.

- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria): Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids: Not performed.
- Cervical screening: Not discussed.
- STI screen: Not discussed.
- Mammogram: Not discussed.
- Other pathology: None ordered.

Management Plan

- Advised immediate hospital attendance for assessment of possible postpartum pulmonary embolism.  
- Offered ambulance; patient opted to self-present with infant.  
- Instructed to bring necessary items for baby and to travel promptly.  
- Advised to withhold Codeine until evaluated.  
- Explained risk of clots post-C-section and potential hospital treatments (e.g., anticoagulation).  
- No additional prescriptions, investigations, or referrals arranged during call.

Consider (not arranged during consult):

- Formal ED referral letter or phone handover.  
- Post-discharge follow-up with GP/AMS for VTE prophylaxis review, wound check, contraception, and routine postpartum care.  
- CTG registration and preventive health catch-up when stable.  
- Allied health/Mental health support if stress persists.

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: BP, detailed pulse rate/rhythm, height/weight/BMI, waist circumference, full medication list, allergy reaction description, immunisation review, smoking/alcohol/substance history, diet and exercise assessment, mental health screening, hearing and vision screening, urinalysis, baseline blood tests.  
● Internal contradictions: Date of birth given as 20 Apr 1980 by patient; clinician later repeated “1983” – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; exact duration of pulse count not specified; some minor omissions typical of urgent telehealth consult.
